newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Issing seeks strong EMU stability pact.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Issing seeks strong EMU stability pact.

text.p: Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing said on Monday that it was more important to negotiate a strong stability pact to ensure fiscal discipline under the Euro than opt for a weaker but speedier deal.
Issing told Reuters Financial Television: "Germany insists that content (when it comes to a stability pact) is more important than time."
He also said he did not think France and Germany were currently at odds over the stability pact and the two would ultimately agree on the details of formulating the structures of a stability package.
"In the end I expect we will come to a peaceful agreement on the pact," he said.
He also said any exemptions from the pact should be clearly formulated to prevent the pact from falling victim to political wrangling.
When asked about French calls for Germany to lower its interest rates further, Issing said there were currently "no changes in opinion between the two central banks."
